summary: First call: he ran a family bakery for almost thirty years, then managed production at a commercial bread plant.

turns.text: Hi Walter, I'm Pip from Memoria. I'll call once a week to hear your stories. Tell me about your very first job.
My father's bakery on 5th Street. I started at twelve, kneading dough before school. Took it over in 1962 and ran it until 1990.
The supermarkets got us. I sold the shop and went to run production at Golden Crust, the big bread plant in Fresno. Eighty people on my shifts.
What were you best known for there?
Scheduling. Getting forty thousand loaves out the door with no waste. And training the young ones. I don't want to talk about the strike in '94 though, that was a bad time.
Of course. What would you tell someone starting out in food production today?
Learn every machine yourself before you manage people who run them. And always have a plan B.
